The sunnah of this day: enter ihram, head to Mina and spend the night there, repeating the Talbiyah "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk", and pray there shortened without combining.
The greatest pillar: stand at Arafah from after noon until sunset, making much supplication, takbir and tahlil. The Prophet (PBUH) said: "Hajj is Arafah."
Eid al-Adha: stone Jamarat al-Aqabah with seven pebbles, offer the sacrifice, shave or trim, then perform Tawaf al-Ifadah and Sai.
Stone the three Jamarat after noon: the small, then the middle, then the large, seven pebbles each while saying takbir, supplicating after the small and middle ones.
Repeat stoning the three Jamarat after noon as yesterday. Whoever wishes to hasten may leave Mina before sunset; whoever stays spends the night and stones on the third day.
Stone the three Jamarat after noon, then conclude the Hajj with the farewell Tawaf when leaving Makkah. May Allah accept your Hajj.

A written will helps preserve rights and organise what family members may need after a death. Record important information in a private draft, save it on your device, or choose to share it with trusted people.

Important: this is an organisational and educational tool, not an enforceable legal will or a ruling for your circumstances. Consult a qualified scholar and a lawyer or notary before relying on it, especially for debts, inheritance, and financial bequests.
Privacy: the draft is saved locally on this device. The app does not upload or share it automatically. Verify the recipient and sharing method before sending.

This educational tool displays a GPS distance reference. It does not issue a personal ruling on shortening or combining prayers; distance, route, intended stay, and school differences require guidance from a trusted scholarly authority.
A GPS fix is requested only when you tap the button. The departure point is stored on this device; there is no background tracking or location upload.

This preview uses the existing calculation engine and saved high-latitude rule. When Fajr or Isha signs disappear, multiple methods and scholarly positions exist; follow your mosque’s timetable or the recognised authority in your country.
Add a prayer location and its time zone in Prayer Settings to view the preview.
The engine cannot produce a consistent set of times for this date and location. Select a local-authority timetable or seek scholarly guidance on the adopted estimation.
Add a location to show its high-latitude band.
Zone one: below 48°; astronomical signs normally appear, but follow your local authority’s timetable.
Zone two: 48° to below 66°; some Fajr or Isha signs may be absent on some days of the year.
Zone three: 66° and above; signs may be absent for long periods, so an adopted scholarly estimation is essential.
